name: Wanaka Town Center and Lakefront
tagline: The heart of it all, steps from the water
description: The compact hub around Ardmore Street and the lakeshore, where cafes, shops, restaurants and the marina cluster beside Lake Wanaka. Walkable, lively in season and blessed with postcard views, it is the most convenient and social place to base yourself, if you can secure a rental.
bestFor: Nomads wanting walkable convenience, cafes and lake views on the doorstep
pros: Walk to cafes, coworking-friendly spots and the lakefront
Best selection of dining, shops and services
cons: Busy and touristy at peak times

name: Albert Town
tagline: Riverside living a few minutes from town
description: A relaxed residential area by the Clutha River, a short drive or bike ride from central Wanaka. Popular with families and long-term locals, it offers river swimming spots, quiet streets and easy trail access, trading lakefront buzz for a calmer, more settled everyday pace.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads wanting calm, space and river access near town
pros: Riverside walks and swimming on the Clutha
Quieter and more residential than the center
Quick drive or cycle into Wanaka
cons: Fewer cafes and amenities on the doorstep
A car or bike is handy for daily errands

name: Cardrona and the Valley
tagline: Alpine base toward the ski fields
description: The rural valley climbing south toward the Cardrona ski field and the historic Cardrona settlement, with its famous heritage hotel. Sparse, scenic and cold in winter, it suits those wanting mountain seclusion and ski-season proximity over town convenience, connected by a winding mountain road.
bestFor: Ski-focused, solitude-seeking nomads who do not mind a commute
pros: Historic Cardrona Hotel and valley charm
cons: Remote, with a winding road that needs winter care

name: Lake Hawea
description: A smaller, more low-key township on the shore of Lake Hawea, about fifteen minutes from Wanaka. It offers the same alpine-and-lake beauty with fewer crowds and a slower rhythm, appealing to nomads who want peace and nature while staying within reach of Wanaka's amenities.
bestFor: Nature-first nomads wanting quiet lakeside living near Wanaka
pros: Calmer and often better value than central Wanaka
Easy hikes and water access from the doorstep
cons: Need to drive to Wanaka for most services
